title: Aspect Deep 6: Хотеть, Любить, Мочь and the Infinitive
titleRussian: Виды глагола 6: Хотеть, любить, мочь + инфинитив
description: Verbs of desire, preference, and ability default to imperfective infinitives. The perfective appears when there is a specific bounded result in mind.
descriptionRussian: Глаголы желания, предпочтения и возможности (хотеть, любить, мочь) по умолчанию требуют инфинитива НСВ. СВ появляется, когда речь идёт о конкретном результате.
intro: Unlike the phase verbs, these do give you a choice, and the default is imperfective. Wanting, liking and being able are general states, and general states pair with general activities. But when you have one specific finished thing in mind, the perfective comes back. One of these verbs almost never takes it, because a standing preference cannot be about a single completed event.
rules: Хотеть, любить, нравиться, и мочь take an IMPERFECTIVE infinitive by default. This covers general desire, preference, habit, and ability.
When the speaker has a SPECIFIC bounded result in mind (a single completed object, a deadline, a one-shot completion claim), the perfective infinitive appears.
Любить almost always takes the imperfective: a general preference cannot pair with a single completed event.
Diagnostic question: is this a general activity (love, habit, ability), or a specific bounded result? General → impf; specific result → pf.
examples: Я люблю читать книги по вечерам. (I love reading books in the evenings.) Любить + impf: general preference.
Маша хочет смотреть фильмы каждый вечер. (Masha wants to watch films every evening.) Хотеть + impf: habit.
Я хочу прочитать эту книгу до конца месяца. (I (m) want to read this book through by the end of the month.) Хотеть + pf: specific bounded plan.
Маша хочет написать статью к понедельнику. (Masha wants to write the article by Monday.) Хотеть + pf: deadline.
Антон может писать стихи на двух языках. (Anton can write poetry in two languages.) Мочь + impf: general ability.
Лена не любит говорить долго по телефону. (Lena doesn't like talking on the phone for long.) Любить + impf: general preference + duration cue.

rows.label: хотеть
cells: Specific bounded plan, deadline, single object → pf

rows.label: любить
cells: Almost never; preference for one-shot events is unusual

rows.label: мочь
cells: Ability to complete one specific bounded action → pf

rows.label: нравиться + dat
cells: Almost never; the construction is preference-based

items.promptEnglish: Masha started reading a long novel.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 5: phase verbs take which infinitive?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 5: phase verbs like начать take only the imperfective infinitive. Начала + читать. Today's lesson moves to MODAL verbs (хотеть, любить, мочь), where the default is also the imperfective, but the perfective is allowed under specific conditions.

items.promptEnglish: I love drinking coffee in the mornings.
items.hint: Любить + infinitive: general preference. Which aspect?
items.explanation: Любить expresses a general preference and almost always takes an imperfective infinitive. Любить + пить. The frequency cue 'по утрам' reinforces the habitual reading. The perfective выпить would describe a single completed drinking, which 'love drinking' cannot pair with.

items.prompt: Маша хочет _____ эту книгу до выходных.
items.promptEnglish: Masha wants to read this book through by the weekend.
items.hint: Specific book + deadline. Specific bounded plan → which infinitive aspect?
items.explanation: A specific object ('эту книгу') plus a deadline ('до выходных') creates a bounded completion plan. With хотеть, this picture takes the perfective infinitive: хочет + прочитать. The imperfective читать would describe a general wish to be reading, which the deadline rules out.

items.prompt: Антон любит _____ статьи в этом журнале.
items.promptEnglish: Anton loves reading articles in this magazine.
items.hint: Любить + infinitive: which aspect by default?
items.explanation: Любить is a verb of general preference and takes an imperfective infinitive. Любит + читать. The plural object 'статьи' (articles, no specific one) reinforces the general reading. The perfective прочитать would describe one specific article being read through, which the general preference does not target.

items.prompt: Я хочу _____ новую статью к понедельнику.
items.promptEnglish: I (m) want to write a new article by Monday.
items.explanation: A specific article ('новую статью') plus a deadline ('к понедельнику') is a bounded completion plan. Хотеть + perfective infinitive: хочу + написать. The imperfective писать would describe a general wish to be writing, which the deadline cue rules out.

items.prompt: Лена не любит _____ долго по телефону.
items.promptEnglish: Lena doesn't like talking on the phone for a long time.
items.explanation: Любить by itself prefers the imperfective. The duration cue 'долго' (recap from A2 Aspect Intro Lesson 4) further reinforces the imperfective. Не любит + говорить. The perfective сказать would describe a single completed utterance, incompatible both with любить and with 'долго.'
A general preference after любить takes the imperfective infinitive: любит готовить. Приготовить would point to one bounded meal.

items.hint: Не любить + a general manner of acting.
items.explanation: A general preference takes the imperfective infinitive: не любит говорить громко. Сказать is perfective (one utterance).

items.promptEnglish: I want to finish this article tonight.
items.hint: A specific bounded plan with a deadline.
items.explanation: A bounded plan with a deadline takes the perfective infinitive: хочу написать эту статью. Писать would name only the process.
General ability takes the imperfective infinitive: может читать по-русски. Прочитать would claim the ability to finish one specific text.

items.promptEnglish: Anton can read this book through in two days.
items.hint: Ability to complete one bounded action.
items.explanation: The ability to complete one specific book within a set time takes the perfective infinitive: может прочитать эту книгу за два дня. Читать would name open-ended reading with no completion.

blanks: Маша любит _____ обед всей семье по воскресеньям. (Masha loves cooking dinner for the whole family on Sundays.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Любить is a verb of general preference and takes an imperfective infinitive. The 'по воскресеньям' habitual frame (Lesson 2) reinforces the impf. Любит + готовить. The perfective приготовить would describe a single completed Sunday dinner, which the habitual frame rules out.

errorCorrection.sentence: Дедушка любит рассказать смешные истории внукам.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Grandpa loves telling funny stories to his grandchildren.
errorCorrection.explanation: Любить expresses a general preference and almost always takes an imperfective infinitive: любит рассказывать. The perfective рассказать ('tell one story to the end') names a single completed act, which you cannot 'love' the way you love a recurring activity. Любить is the strictest of the modal verbs: a one-shot completion almost never fits it.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша хочет покупать новый телефон до конца месяца.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha wants to buy a new phone by the end of the month.
errorCorrection.explanation: A specific object ('новый телефон') plus a deadline ('до конца месяца') is a bounded completion plan, so хотеть takes the perfective infinitive: хочет купить. The imperfective покупать would describe a general wish to be shopping for phones, which a one-time deadline rules out. Хотеть is the most flexible modal verb: imperfective for a general wish, perfective when a specific result is in view.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон может решать эту задачу за пять минут.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton can solve this problem in five minutes.
errorCorrection.explanation: With мочь, the perfective infinitive appears when the meaning is the ability to complete one specific bounded action. 'Эту задачу за пять минут' (this problem within five minutes) is a bounded completion, so the perfective решить is required.

minimalPairs.context: Я хочу _____ статью за один вечер.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I (m) want to write an article in a single evening.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'За один вечер' measures the time the job takes to be finished, so the plan is bounded: хочу написать. The imperfective писать would describe a general wish to be writing, which the 'за + acc' phrase rules out.

Любить is a verb of general preference and takes an imperfective infinitive. Люблю писать. The perfective написать would target one specific completed article, which 'love writing articles' cannot pair with.

reviewVocab.definition: to want (modal-style verb; takes an imperfective infinitive by default, perfective when a specific bounded result is in mind: 'хочу прочитать эту книгу')
reviewVocab.example: Я хочу прочитать эту книгу до выходных.

reviewVocab.definition: to love, to like to do (modal-style verb of general preference; takes an imperfective infinitive almost without exception)
to be able to (modal verb; takes an imperfective infinitive for general ability, perfective for ability to complete one bounded action)
reviewVocab.example: Антон может прочитать всю книгу за один день.
